title: The closed-support triangle at every coefficient stage
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ invertible in the field $k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$, as in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. In the Weil clause use the finite-field datum of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be
a closed immersion and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ the complementary open
immersion. Let $\Lambda$ be one of the coefficient stages
$A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb$, with the categories $D^b_c(-,\Lambda)$ of
[def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed],
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi],
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], the pullbacks of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the direct images $i_*$, $Rj_*$
of [def-weil-derived-direct-image].

1. $Rj_*$ carries $D^b_c(U,\Lambda)$ into $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$.
2. $i_*:D^b_c(Z,\Lambda)\to D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ has a right adjoint $Ri^!$;
   it is the exceptional inverse image of
   [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] (at $\mathcal O_E$ it is
   $R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nRi_n^!K_n$, with reductions
   $Ri_n^!K_n$).
3. For $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ the closed exceptional counit and the open
   unit extend to a distinguished triangle
   $$
   i_*Ri^!K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow Rj_*j^*K
   \longrightarrow i_*Ri^!K[1],
   $$
   with $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*Ri^!K[m],Rj_*j^*K)=0$ for all $m$, so the
   third arrow is unique and the triangle is functorial in $K$.
4. $Ri^!Rj_*G=0$ for $G\in D^b_c(U,\Lambda)$, and the unit
   $Q\to Ri^!i_*Q$ is an isomorphism for $Q\in D^b_c(Z,\Lambda)$.

The same holds on the finite-Tor subcategories $D^b_{ctf}(-,\Lambda)$ of
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Let $d=\dim U$ when $U\ne\varnothing$ and put $d=0$ when $U=\varnothing$, using the Krull dimension of [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Assume
$c=\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(k)$ ([def-sc-etale-torsion-cd]) is finite
($c=0$ for $k$ algebraically closed).

- (1') $Rj_*$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(U,\Lambda)$ into $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$;
   at $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ goes to Tor amplitude in
   $[a,b+2d+c]$, and at $\mathcal O_E$ the same holds for the uniform
   interval of the reductions.
- (2') $Ri^!$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ into $D^b_{ctf}(Z,\Lambda)$,
   with Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ going to $[a,b+2d+c+1]$ (at $A_{E,n}$, and
   uniformly in the reductions at $\mathcal O_E$).
- (3') $i_*$, $i^*$ and $j^*$ preserve $D^b_{ctf}$ and Tor amplitude
   intervals; hence for $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ all three vertices of
   the triangle of (3) lie in $D^b_{ctf}$.
- (4') For $G\in D^b_{ctf}(U,\Lambda)$ and $Q\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,\Lambda)$,
   $Ri^!Rj_*G=0$ and $Q\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri^!i_*Q$ inside $D^b_{ctf}$.

At $E$ and $\Qlb$ these are (1)–(4), since there $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$.

If the complementary immersion pair $(i,j)$ is the base change of a closed immersion $i_0:Z_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ and its open complement $j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ over $k_0$, and $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$, then $Ri^!$
carries Weil structures ([def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]) for which the
adjunction is equivariant, and for Weil complexes the three arrows of the
triangle and the unit are Weil-equivariant.

proof.text: For every finite extension F/Q_l construct an integral localization by [lem-sf-integral-localization-construction]. Select the record at E, and transport it to the rational stage by [lem-sf-rational-localization-construction]. For each finite field L in the algebraically closed index, apply the same two steps at its coefficient field. Descend that family by [lem-sf-common-stage-localization-construction]. The finite stages required in the first conjunct are the fields finiteStages of the chosen integral record. Assemble these four witnesses; no new object is defined by an arbitrary existence choice.

The geometric-fibre map is a pullback of the original immersion. Apply base-change stability to the closed and open immersion properties. For any map over k0, use the Cartesian square of the two geometric-fibre projections: commutativity gives one range inclusion and Scheme.exists_preimage_of_isPullback gives the other. This identifies the range of the fibre map with the inverse image of the original range. Inverse image preserves complement, so the geometric pair is complementary. Apply the ordinary all-stage theorem (the preceding proof step) to obtain rational and common-stage supported localization records. Their closed_pull and open_pull fields identify the pullbacks with the published ones.

Specialize semilinearFieldOperationLifts to the identity morphism of each of X0, Z0 and U0. Extract the rational and common-stage Frobenius equivalences and an exact shift structure on the X functor. Transport the canonical fieldWeilPullSquare and zlFrobeniusSquare isomorphisms along the equalities identifying the supported pullbacks.

For a supported record S, write P,Q,H for the three Frobenius equivalences and d,dj for the two pullback comparisons. Form a=IsoAlgebra.mateIso(S.closedAdjunction,d), b=mateIso(S.exceptionalAdjunction,a), and r=mateIso(S.openAdjunction,dj). Invertibility follows from the equivalence version of mateIso. Apply mapOfNatIsoAdjunction to the exceptional and open adjunctions. Its proved unit/counit formulas give exactly the required carrier arrows, and the three transport functors have definitionally the required composites with forgetful functors. Lift shift by mapOfNatIso(P.commShiftIso 1).

For a Weil object K let e1,e2,e3 be the closed, middle and open structure isomorphisms. The proved mate unit/counit identities give the first two squares. Set delta=e3 inverse followed by P(boundary), the Frobenius shift comparison and the shift of e1. Triangle.isoMk gives an isomorphism from the P-image of the supported distinguished triangle to the triangle with the original first two arrows and delta. Exactness makes this distinguished. The unique_boundary field forces delta=boundary, which after cancellation is precisely the third Weil square. This gives the boundary component as a fixed-pair morphism. Its naturality is the original boundary naturality on carriers, using faithfulness. Assemble SfWeilLocalization and the two existential witnesses with their original pullback equalities.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be
a closed immersion and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ the complementary open
immersion. Let $\Lambda$ be one of the coefficient rings
$A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb$, regarded as condensed rings, with the
categories $D^b_c(-,\Lambda)\subseteq D(-_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ of
[def-sf-setting], the pullbacks of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]
and the direct images $i_*$, $Rj_*$ of $\Lambda$-modules
([def-weil-derived-direct-image], [det-def-sf-operations]).

1. $Rj_*$ carries $D^b_c(U,\Lambda)$ into $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$.
2. $i_*:D^b_c(Z,\Lambda)\to D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ has a right adjoint $Ri^!$;
   it is the exceptional inverse image of
   [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] at $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, and of
   [sk-thm-existence] in general. At $\mathcal O_E$ its reductions are
   $(Ri^!K)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,m}\cong Ri_m^!K_m$.
3. For $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ the closed exceptional counit and the open
   unit extend to a distinguished triangle
   $$
   i_*Ri^!K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow Rj_*j^*K
   \longrightarrow i_*Ri^!K[1],
   $$
   with $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*Ri^!K[m],Rj_*j^*K)=0$ for all $m$, so the
   third arrow is unique and the triangle is functorial in $K$.
4. $Ri^!Rj_*G=0$ for $G\in D^b_c(U,\Lambda)$, and the unit
   $Q\to Ri^!i_*Q$ is an isomorphism for $Q\in D^b_c(Z,\Lambda)$.

The same holds on the finite-Tor subcategories $D^b_{ctf}(-,\Lambda)$ of
[def-sf-setting] and [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Let $d=\dim U$ and assume
$c=\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(k)$ ([def-sc-etale-torsion-cd]) is finite
($c=0$ for $k$ algebraically closed).

- (1') $Rj_*$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(U,\Lambda)$ into $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$;
   at $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ goes to Tor amplitude in
   $[a,b+2d+c]$, and at $\mathcal O_E$ the same holds for the uniform
   interval of the reductions.
- (2') $Ri^!$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ into $D^b_{ctf}(Z,\Lambda)$,
   with Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ going to $[a,b+2d+c+1]$ (at $A_{E,n}$, and
   uniformly in the reductions at $\mathcal O_E$).
- (3') $i_*$, $i^*$ and $j^*$ preserve $D^b_{ctf}$ and Tor amplitude
   intervals; hence for $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ all three vertices of
   the triangle of (3) lie in $D^b_{ctf}$.
- (4') For $G\in D^b_{ctf}(U,\Lambda)$ and $Q\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,\Lambda)$,
   $Ri^!Rj_*G=0$ and $Q\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri^!i_*Q$ inside $D^b_{ctf}$.

At $E$ and $\Qlb$ these are (1)–(4), since there $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ ([lem-integral-ctf-equals-bc]).

If $X,Z,U$ come from $k_0$-schemes and $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$, then $Ri^!$
carries Weil structures ([sk-def-sf-weil-complexes], [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]) for which the
adjunction is equivariant, and for Weil complexes the three arrows of the
triangle and the unit are Weil-equivariant.

proof.text:
*Vanishing.* For every $\Lambda$, $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*P[m],Rj_*N)=0$ for
$P\in D(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ and $N\in D(U_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$. Indeed
it is $\operatorname{Hom}(j^*i_*P[m],N)$ by $j^*\dashv Rj_*$
([def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], [det-def-sf-operations]), and
$j^*i_*=0$: $j^*$ is restriction to $U_{\mathrm{proét}}$, and
$(i_*M)(V)=M(V\times_XZ)=0$ for $V$ over $U$ (compare
[lem-exc-proetale-closed-essential-image]). Moreover $j^*Rj_*\cong\operatorname{id}$.
Indeed $j^*$ is restriction to the localization of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ at
the object $U$, which preserves K-injective complexes
([Tag 08FI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08FI)). Since
$U\times_XU=U$, the square with two sides $j$ and two sides
$\operatorname{id}_U$ is cartesian, and base change for localizations
([Tag 0FN5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FN5)) gives
$j^*Rj_*\cong R(\operatorname{id}_U)_*\operatorname{id}_U^*=\operatorname{id}$.

*(1).* For $\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$ one has $D^b_c=D^b_{ctf}$, and $Rj_*$
preserves it ([sk-thm-sf-ctf-stability]). For $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$, write
$G=\nu_U^*G'$ with $G'$ étale bounded constructible
([lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]); then $Rj_*G\cong\nu_X^*Rj_*G'$ by
[prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image], and $Rj_*G'$ is bounded constructible
by [thm-fin-open-immersion] and dévissage over the finitely many cohomology
sheaves ([thm-constructible-serre]).

*(2) and (3).* The argument is the same for every $\Lambda$. Let
$K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and let $F\to K\to Rj_*j^*K\to F[1]$ be a fibre
sequence of the open unit. By (1), $F\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$
([det-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]). Since $j^*K\to j^*Rj_*j^*K$ is an
isomorphism, $j^*F=0$. The open–closed triangle
[prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages] for $F$ then shows that the unit
$F\to i_*i^*F$ is an isomorphism. Put $Q=i^*F\in D^b_c(Z,\Lambda)$. For
$P\in D^b_c(Z,\Lambda)$ the vanishing and the full faithfulness of
[prop-sf-closed-unit-all-stages] give, naturally in $P$,
$$
\operatorname{Hom}(P,Q)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(i_*P,i_*Q)
=\operatorname{Hom}(i_*P,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(i_*P,K).
$$
Thus $Ri^!K:=Q$ is right adjoint to $i_*$ on $D^b_c$, with counit $F\to K$,
and the triangle of (3) is $F\to K\to Rj_*j^*K\to$. The vanishing makes
its third arrow unique and the triangle functorial. By uniqueness of right
adjoints $Ri^!$ is the restriction of the exceptional inverse image of
[sk-thm-existence] ($i_*=Ri_!$, $i$ being proper). At $\Lambda=A$ it is
also the restriction of the ambient right adjoint of
[lem-exc-proetale-closed-support], with the triangle of
[lem-exc-proetale-support-triangle], and hence the finite exceptional inverse
image of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], as in
[prop-sf-closed-immersion-unit]. At $\mathcal O_E$ the coefficient
comparisons along $\mathcal O_E\to A_{E,m}$ for $Rj_*$ and for the exceptional
inverse image are isomorphisms ([sk-prop-scalar-six]). This gives
$(Rj_*G)_m\cong Rj_*G_m$ and $(Ri^!K)_m\cong Ri_m^!K_m$; integral models and
reductions enter only here, as consequences.

*Consequences.* For (4): $\operatorname{Hom}(N[m],Ri^!Rj_*G)
=\operatorname{Hom}(i_*N[m],Rj_*G)=0$ for all $N$ and $m$, so
$Ri^!Rj_*G=0$; the unit is an isomorphism by
[prop-sf-closed-unit-all-stages].

*Finite Tor amplitude.* Let $A=A_{E,n}$ and $\kappa=A/(\pi_E)$, the
constant sheaf on each site.

*Residue criterion.* On any of the pro-étale sites, a bounded constructible
complex $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ if and only if $K\otimes^L_A\kappa$
has cohomology in $[a,b]$, by [lem-sf-proetale-residue-tor-test], the
pro-étale form of the étale criterion [lem-exc-residue-tor-test]; it is
applied below only to bounded constructible complexes, by (1) and (2). The pullbacks
$i^*,j^*,\nu^*$ commute with $-\otimes^L_A\kappa$, being monoidal with
$\kappa$ pulling back to $\kappa$ ([def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom],
[lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-unit]); being exact they preserve
cohomological intervals. Conversely $\nu^*$ reflects them: if
$\nu^*C$ has cohomology in $[a,b]$ for $C\in\Dplus$, then
$\nu^*\tau_{>b}C=\tau_{>b}\nu^*C=0$, hence $\tau_{>b}C=0$ by
[thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], and likewise below $a$.

*(3') for $i^*,j^*,i_*$.* For $i^*$ and $j^*$ this is the criterion and
the commutation just stated. For $P\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ with amplitude
$[a,b]$, $j^*(i_*P\otimes^L_A\kappa)\cong j^*i_*P\otimes^L_A\kappa=0$, so
each cohomology sheaf of $i_*P\otimes^L_A\kappa$ is in the image of $i_*$
([lem-exc-proetale-closed-essential-image]) and equals
$i_*i^*\mathcal H^r(i_*P\otimes^L_A\kappa)\cong
i_*\mathcal H^r(P\otimes^L_A\kappa)$, using exactness of $i^*$ and
$i^*i_*\cong\operatorname{id}$; it vanishes outside $[a,b]$.

*(1') at the finite stage.* Let $G\in D^b_{ctf}(U,A)$ have amplitude
$[a,b]$ and write $G=\nu_U^*G'$ as in the proof of (1). Then
$\nu_U^*(G'\otimes^L_A\kappa)\cong G\otimes^L_A\kappa$ has cohomology in
$[a,b]$, hence so has $G'\otimes^L_A\kappa$. The higher direct images
$R^qj_*$ on the small étale site vanish on sheaves of $A$-modules for
$q>2d+c$: for $k$ algebraically closed this is
[lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing]; in general its proof applies
verbatim, with [thm-sc-finite-type-torsion-cd] at the given $c$. By the
truncation spectral sequence [thm-sp-truncation-e2],
$Rj_*(G'\otimes^L_A\kappa)$ has cohomology in $[a,b+2d+c]$.

*Projection formula for $\kappa$.* The canonical map
$Rj_*G'\otimes^L_A\kappa\to Rj_*(G'\otimes^L_A\kappa)$ is an isomorphism.
Choose a bounded-above resolution $P\to\kappa$ by finite free $A$-modules;
tensoring with the constant complex $P$ computes $-\otimes^L_A\kappa$. For
the finite stupid truncations $\sigma_{\ge-t}P$ the comparison is an
isomorphism: it is the identity for $A$ and is preserved by finite sums,
shifts and cones. Let $G'$ and $Rj_*G'$ have cohomology in degrees $\le e$.
The quotients $\sigma_{<-t}P$ live in degrees $\le-t-1$, so
$G'\otimes\sigma_{<-t}P$ has cohomology in degrees $\le e-t-1$, and
$Rj_*$ of it in degrees $\le e-t-1+2d+c$ (the vanishing above), while
$Rj_*G'\otimes\sigma_{<-t}P$ has cohomology in degrees $\le e-t-1$.
For fixed $r$ and $t$ large, the long exact sequences of the two
triangles attached to $\sigma_{\ge-t}P\to P\to\sigma_{<-t}P$ therefore
identify both sides with the finite-free comparison in degree $r$.

Hence $Rj_*G'\otimes^L_A\kappa$ has cohomology in $[a,b+2d+c]$. Applying
$\nu_X^*$ and [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image],
$Rj_*G\otimes^L_A\kappa\cong\nu_X^*(Rj_*G'\otimes^L_A\kappa)$ has
cohomology in the same interval; with (1), the residue criterion gives
$Rj_*G\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ with amplitude $[a,b+2d+c]$.

*(2') at the finite stage.* Let $K$ have amplitude $[a,b]$. Then $j^*K$
has amplitude $[a,b]$ and $Rj_*j^*K$ amplitude $[a,b+2d+c]$. Tensoring the
triangle of (3) with $\kappa$ and taking the long exact sequence,
$\mathcal H^r(i_*Ri^!K\otimes^L_A\kappa)$ lies between
$\mathcal H^{r-1}(Rj_*j^*K\otimes^L_A\kappa)$ and
$\mathcal H^r(K\otimes^L_A\kappa)$, so it vanishes outside
$[a,b+2d+c+1]$. Since $Ri^!K\cong i^*i_*Ri^!K$, the commutation of $i^*$
with $-\otimes^L_A\kappa$ and the residue criterion give amplitude
$[a,b+2d+c+1]$ for $Ri^!K$.

*Other stages.* At $\mathcal O_E$, the reductions are
$(Rj_*G)_m\cong Rj_*G_m$ and $(Ri^!K)_m\cong Ri_m^!K_m$ (shown above), and
similarly for $i^*,j^*,i_*$; the finite-stage bounds hold with intervals
depending only on the uniform interval of the reductions of $G$, resp. $K$.
At $E$ and $\Qlb$, $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ ([lem-integral-ctf-equals-bc]). Clauses (3') and
(4') are then (3) and (4) read inside the full subcategories $D^b_{ctf}$.

*Weil structures.* The Weil structures of $i^*,j^*,Rj_*$ come from the
exchange isomorphisms for the Frobenius automorphism squares, and the open
unit is equivariant, as in [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages]. For a Weil complex $K$, the
fibre $F$ therefore carries a unique Weil structure making $F\to K$
equivariant (uniqueness from the vanishing), and $Ri^!K=i^*F$ inherits it;
under the adjunction bijection above this is the mate of the Weil structure
of $i_*$, so the adjunction, its counit and unit are equivariant. The third
arrow is equivariant by the uniqueness in (3).
